summary.headline: Sansera Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR10,915m (+32% YoY) with EBITDA INR2,112m (+48%) and 19.4% margin despite cost headwinds.
summary.overview: Sansera posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR10,915m, up 32% YoY, with EBITDA up 48% to INR2,112m and PAT up 52% to INR1,086m. Gross margin expanded 180bps to 43% on mix, while Karnataka minimum wage revision (INR167m provision) and freight/tariff costs weighed on other expenses. ADS (non-auto) crossed INR2,000m in a quarter for the first time at 20.9% of sales, and the ADS backlog rose to INR58.7bn from INR44.4bn in June. Net debt rose to INR2,612m from INR604m in March as capex was raised to INR8,000m for FY27. Management guided FY27 revenue to INR42,500-43,000m.

segments.name: Auto ICE
segments.commentary: Quarterly sales INR6,697m, +18% YoY, with passenger vehicles, two-wheeler motorcycles and scooters each posting record quarterly sales. Auto ICE is about 65% of total sales.

segments.name: Auto-Tech Agnostic and xEV
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarterly sales, combined INR1,363m in Q2 FY27.

segments.name: ADS (aerospace, defence, semicon)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR1,643m; H1 INR3,097m. Non-automotive segment crossed INR2,000m in the quarter (20.9% of sales). Backlog INR58.7bn executable over five years; a large multi-year semicon order was added.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue indicated at INR4,250-4,300 crores (INR42,500-43,000m), with H2 healthy but dependent on post-festive industry performance and the West Asia conflict; whether H2 exceeds H1 (INR21,127m) is uncertain.
FY27 capex projection raised to about INR8,000m (from about INR5,000-5,800m earlier); about 50% (~INR4,000m) to ADS.
Sansera-Nichidai JV commercial or sample production expected towards end of Q4 FY27 (also described as end H2 FY27); three forging press lines to be commissioned initially.
Aerospace facility fully operational by Q3 FY27; defence facility operational towards end Q3 or from Q4 FY27; new facility planned towards end of calendar 2027.
ADS target of 35-40% of Sansera revenue by end of decade; company aspiration of INR8,000 crore revenue by FY30 reiterated; new vision and targets to be set around year end.
Karnataka minimum wage provision expected to continue (not one-off), with exact quantum still provisional; expected increase about INR5,500 or ~30% in base wages for affected workers.
Sweden operations expected steady at 80-85% efficiency; target EBITDA 10-12%.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex raised to about INR8,000m (from INR500-800 crore range cited on call), with about 50% going to ADS; second bay of existing plant construction completed and being filled with machines.

ADS capacity: current plant 9 expansion supports about INR1,500 crore revenue; another facility could add INR1,000-1,500 crore; defence facility about INR400-500 crore. Preetham referred to INR3,500 crore potential capacity.
Aerospace facility (new ~120,000 sq ft facility announced nearby) to be operational by Q3 FY27 with expanded bay; defence capex about INR15-20 crore if orders materialise.
Nichidai JV (steering driveline and related parts, near-net-shape forging) to commission three forging press lines to begin with.
US manufacturing plant (mainly connecting rods) placed on hold; board reassessing risks; Sansera prefers India outsourcing if it materialises.
demand_pricing: Domestic PV wholesale crossed 5 lakh units in a month for the first time in October; OEM order backlogs and lean dealer inventories give visibility into Q3 FY27.

Non-auto order book (ex-ADS) INR22.4bn, about half domestic (49%, up from 44% in June); PV orders mainly from North America and Europe, with new engine programmes from a North American export customer built in India.
Semicon: still a single customer; a second customer targeted in Q3 FY27. Aerospace: a couple of new customers added; first business from Safran won this quarter (not blisk or rotating parts).
Engine blisk development with a customer progressing on pre-agreed milestones, development conclusion expected Q3 FY27; Rolls-Royce rotating component development also expected to finish Q3.
Two-wheeler OEM insourcing reversal: pilot order won with one OEM, scale-up pending execution.
Cost pressure: West Asia conflict raised cutting tool, freight and logistics costs; management pursuing customer pass-through, with commodity impacts not yet recovered.

qa_highlights.question: Which segments and customers drove the non-ADS order book increase?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is equally split domestic and export, skewed to PVs; no big new customers added. Gains came from a North American export customer's engine programmes built in India, a new tractor customer, and PV engine nominations from existing customers.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ADS backlog jumped while still described as executable over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Hari Krishnan said the INR58.7bn is confirmed orders executable over five years; Preetham said ADS orders are spread across years one to four, so new bookings lift revenue in following years.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split between semicon and aerospace and whether run-rate sustains?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said lead times have shortened as new-sector programmes (semicon, energy, xEV) start faster; FY27 capex raised from INR500-800 crore range to accommodate, with about half to ADS. Rolls-Royce-related capex is not included until a confirmed order.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Goel said it included logistics and tariff costs booked last quarter plus freight inflation.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term ADS revenue scenarios and FY30 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham targets ADS at 35-40% of group revenue towards end of decade; FY30 INR8,000 crore aspiration reiterated, with a new vision to be set by year end.

qa_highlights.question: Is MMRFIC included in growth projections and what is capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said MMRFIC (associate, ~47% post CCPS conversion) is excluded from the growth and INR800 crore capex plan; no significant MMRFIC capex planned.

qa_highlights.question: Plans for overseas plant and acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Hari Krishnan said the US plant plan is on hold given tariff uncertainty and board risk review; increased Indian outsourcing is preferred. Preetham said inorganic options are being evaluated, including JVs.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Sweden revenue fall QoQ and what is the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Preetham said the Q2 drop reflects the European summer shutdown; Sweden runs seven days at 80-85% efficiency, October was strong, and H2 is expected steadier and stronger. Hari Krishnan said Sweden depends on one large customer.

qa_highlights.question: Why are finance costs rising and where do they stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Vikas Goel said finance cost is linked to growth, working capital and capex; it may rise slightly further but remains at a healthy level.

risks_watch: Cost headwinds: Karnataka minimum wage provision (INR167m in Q2), freight, cutting tools and tariffs; recovery from customers not yet secured.
Rising leverage: net debt INR2,612m, working capital at 19.6% of annualised Q2 revenue, finance cost up YoY and QoQ.
Execution risk on new ADS facilities (aerospace Q3 FY27, defence Q3/Q4, new plant end-CY27) and JV commissioning at end of Q4 FY27.
Pending qualifications: engine blisk and Rolls-Royce component development expected Q3 FY27; semicon second customer targeted Q3 FY27 but not yet concluded.
Legal and labour code risk: minimum wage revision is provisional and under court challenge; further Labour Code impact under monitoring.
Dependency on single customer at Sansera Sweden and on single semicon customer; Europe volumes.
key_quotes: I am pleased to report another strong quarter for Sansera, with the highest ever quarterly revenue of INR10,915 million, up 32% year-on-year.
So, in the quarters to come, we expect that this order book will further grow substantially.
The lead time for investment has come down because the programs are kick-starting much faster.
But the key thing is for us to demonstrate our readiness with the machines being ready for operation, which is happening right now.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, ADS growth and the record quarter, with a stated aspiration of INR8,000 crore by FY30. Cautious and hedged on H2 revenue (whether it surpasses H1 depends on post-festive industry performance and the West Asia conflict), on the Rolls-Royce opportunity (not yet in capex), and on the timing of the blisk validation and the semicon second customer. Evasive on the size of the Rolls-Royce opportunity and on the exact Karnataka minimum wage quantum, which is still provisional.

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided to INR42,500-43,000m (roughly 14-16% growth implied by H1 of INR21,127m, though H2 vs H1 is uncertain), backed by a INR58.7bn ADS lifetime order book, a INR22.4bn non-ADS order book, and ADS capacity coming online from Q3 FY27 and a second plant bay in trial runs; the aerospace and defence facilities and the Nichidai JV are concrete but timed to FY27-end or later.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Gross margin up 180bps YoY to 43% and EBITDA margin 19.4% (+200bps YoY), but Karnataka minimum wage provision (INR167m) and freight/tariff costs are unrecovered from customers and weigh on other expenses.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Aerospace facility (~120,000 sq ft) fully operational by Q3 FY27, defence facility by end Q3 or Q4 FY27, and Nichidai JV forging lines at end Q4 FY27; second plant bay already in trial runs with FY27 capex raised to INR8,000m.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue up 32% YoY to INR10,915m, ADS backlog INR58.7bn (from INR44.4bn in June) and non-ADS order book INR22.4bn; but H2 vs H1 (INR21,127m) is uncertain on post-festive demand and West Asia conflict.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation at 80-85% with FY27 capex already raised to INR8,000m, and the plan to reach INR8,000 crore revenue by FY30 needs further capacity; new vision and targets to be set around year end.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue guided at INR42,500-43,000m implies only ~14-16% growth on H1 of INR21,127m (+33% YoY), and management is hedged on whether H2 exceeds H1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 is hedged on post-festive industry performance and West Asia conflict; cost pass-through not yet secured and the minimum wage provision could persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Engine blisk and Rolls-Royce rotating component development expected to conclude Q3 FY27, second semicon customer targeted Q3 FY27, and two-wheeler insourcing reversal pilot awaits scale-up; none yet concluded.

rows.label: ADS lifetime order book INR58.7bn
rows.why: Backlog rose to INR58.7bn from INR44.4bn in June (+32%), with orders spread over years one to four so new bookings lift revenue in following years; ADS was INR3,097m in H1.

rows.label: Rising leverage from capex
rows.why: Net debt rose to INR2,612m from INR604m in March and H1 capex plus JV (INR3,560m) exceeded operating cash flow (INR2,073m) by ~INR1,487m, with FY27 capex at INR8,000m; finance costs expected to rise slightly further.

rows.label: ADS target 35-40% of revenue by end of decade
rows.why: ADS was 20.9% of Q2 sales (INR1,643m); reaching 35-40% depends on the aerospace, defence and semicon facilities coming on stream and the INR58.7bn backlog converting.
